correctness.rationale: The formulas are correct. In the Gaussian normalization K_w(z)=exp(z conjugate(w)), the kernel adjoint identity gives C_ψ* f(z)=exp(conjugate(d)z)f(conjugate(c)z). Applying this in the two orders gives the displayed W_{β,q,t,γ} tuples: (a conjugate(d),b conjugate(c),b conjugate(d)) and (conjugate(d),b,0). For such W, the proposed displacements satisfy conjugate(u)+q conjugate(v)=β and −qu−v=t, and changing variables in the Gaussian integral shows these displacements are unitary. Given v=−t−qu, the real part of (|u|²+|v|²)/2+q conjugate(v)u is |t|²/2+Δ|u|²/2. The diagonal dilation has exactly the singular sequence |q|^n, with rank one at q=0; thus substitution and geometric summation give all the stated formulas including the p<1 quasi-norms. Independently, expanding the ratio exponent gives the stated Q/(2Δ). Completing the square gives Q=(1−|c|²)|b−(1−q)d/(1−|c|²)|²−|a−c|²|d|²/(1−|c|²). This verifies the determinant, all three order relations for distinct slopes, and the exact rigidity for equal slopes. Read VERIFICATION.md and verification.py without running the frozen program; the operator proof is exact and not dependent on truncation.

The residual paired order sign is the expansion and completion of the square in the difference of these two known log-norm expressions. The exact paired presentation was not located earlier, but there is no distinct scientific step in it beyond applying existing formulas and elementary algebra; this is prior coverage by implication, not a finding that the frozen claim is false.
